flowchart.name: Flowchart
flowchart.description: Shows the order of steps and decisions in a process.
flowchart.example: The steps and decisions in a login check.

activity.name: UML Activity Diagram
activity.description: Shows activities, decision branches, and tasks that run in parallel.
activity.example: An order workflow that checks payment and stock in parallel.

bpmn.name: BPMN Diagram
bpmn.description: Uses standard symbols to show business activities, events, decisions, and messages.
bpmn.example: A purchase approval process across two departments.

swimlane.name: Swimlane Diagram
swimlane.description: Groups process steps into lanes by person, role, or team.
swimlane.example: A support workflow with lanes for the customer, agent, and manager.

use-case.name: UML Use Case Diagram
use-case.description: Shows how users and other actors achieve goals through a system.
use-case.example: Customers place orders and administrators manage products.

sequence.name: UML Sequence Diagram
sequence.description: Shows the order of messages exchanged between participants.
sequence.example: A browser sends a request to an API, which queries a database.

communication.name: UML Communication Diagram
communication.description: Shows how objects are linked and numbers the messages they exchange.
communication.example: The links and messages between objects during checkout.

timing.name: UML Timing Diagram
timing.description: Shows when states or values change and how long they last.
timing.example: A device becomes active and returns to idle after a timeout.

user-flow.name: User Flow Diagram
user-flow.description: Shows the paths and choices users encounter in an interface.
user-flow.example: A shopper moves from a product listing to checkout.

system-context.name: C4 System Context Diagram
system-context.description: Shows how a system connects to its users and external systems.
system-context.example: An online store connects to customers and a payment provider.

state.name: UML State Machine Diagram
state.description: Shows the states an entity can be in and what triggers transitions.
state.example: An order moves from pending to paid, then to shipped, or it is canceled.

decision-tree.name: Decision Tree
decision-tree.description: Uses branches to show how each decision leads to an outcome.
decision-tree.example: Choosing a support action based on answers to diagnostic questions.

er.name: Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD)
er.description: Shows data entities, their attributes, and how they relate.
er.example: The relationships among customers, orders, and products in a database.

dfd.name: Data Flow Diagram (DFD)
dfd.description: Shows how data moves between processes, stores, and external entities.
dfd.example: A customer submits order details for processing and storage.

tree.name: Tree Diagram
tree.description: Shows how elements are nested through parent-child relationships.

class.name: UML Class Diagram
class.description: Shows software classes, their attributes and operations, and how they relate.
class.example: Product, Cart, and Order classes in a shopping application.

object.name: UML Object Diagram
object.description: Shows specific objects and their links at one point in time.
object.example: A customer object linked to its current shopping cart.

package.name: UML Package Diagram
package.description: Groups related model elements into packages and shows their dependencies.
package.example: Dependencies among authentication, catalog, and order packages.

container.name: C4 Container Diagram
container.description: Shows the main applications and data stores within a system and how they communicate.
container.example: A web client, REST API, and PostgreSQL database.

component.name: UML Component Diagram
component.description: Shows software components, their interfaces, and their dependencies.
component.example: Components for authentication, billing, and inventory.

deployment.name: UML Deployment Diagram
deployment.description: Shows which machines or runtime environments host software artifacts.
deployment.example: An application server connected to a database host.

network.name: Network Topology Diagram
network.description: Shows how network devices are arranged and connected.
network.example: Computers, switches, and a router in a local network.

gantt.name: Gantt Chart
gantt.description: Shows when tasks start and finish as bars on a timeline.
gantt.example: The schedule for design, development, and testing.

pert.name: PERT Network Diagram
pert.description: Shows the paths through a project and which tasks depend on others.
pert.example: How implementation and testing affect the release date.

wbs.name: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
wbs.description: Breaks project scope into a hierarchy of deliverables and work packages.
wbs.example: An application project broken into UI, backend, and documentation deliverables.

mind-map.name: Mind Map
mind-map.description: Arranges related ideas in branches around a central topic.
mind-map.example: Brainstorming features for a diagram editor.

concept-map.name: Concept Map
concept-map.description: Uses labeled links to explain how concepts relate to one another.
concept-map.example: How knowledge bases, rules, and inference engines relate.

org-chart.name: Organizational Chart
org-chart.description: Shows positions, teams, and who reports to whom.
org-chart.example: A development team reports to a project manager.
